title: Midnight driver-hang corral — oncall notes and runbook sketch
content:
Overview:

These are the raw on-call notes and a first-pass runbook sketch following repeated midnight driver hangs observed across a small subset of our GPU fleet over the last two weeks. The behavior is distinct from previous "soft ECC blips" in that the GPU process threads stop making forward progress (no new CUDA kernels scheduled) and the driver watchdog triggers long hangs (~90–300s) followed in some cases by a kernel panic on the host. Hits have clustered on machines with mixed NVLink topologies and a particular kernel/driver combo (Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.1.x, NVIDIA driver 540.XX).

Why this doc exists:
- Capture the real-time triage trail from midnight shifts (notes were noisy);
- Propose reproducible checks and a minimal oncall playbook to contain impact;
- Surface short experiments to validate hypotheses (NVLink negotiation vs driver watchdog vs ECC accumulation);
- Assign next actions for engineering and firmware escalation.

Symptoms observed (consolidated):
- Host-level symptom: sudden spike in driver block time (processes waiting on GPU ioctl), dmesg flooded with "NVRM: Xid" lines and repeated "GPU HANG: kernel driver timeout" entries.
- nvtop/ nvidia-smi show GPU load stuck at constant SM activity but no progress (clock and utilization steady).
- Correctable ECC counters show bursts minutes before hang on some nodes; other nodes show no ECC activity at all.
- NVLink errors (link training fail / negotiation timeouts) logged on a subset; tends to co-occur on boards with 4 x NVLink lanes populated.
- Driver version 540.86 most commonly implicated; older 535.x less noisy on limited sample.

Immediate mitigations taken during incidents:
- Soft-evict affected pods (kube drain for node) to stop new workloads; often processes remain stuck until driver reset.
- Triggered driver reset using nvidia-smi --gpu-reset (where supported) — successes varied (works on PCIe-attached GPUs, fails on some NVLink topologies).
- When host reboot unavoidable, used controlled reboot with kernel parameter nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us=0 to reduce timeout interactions (note: cobbled workaround, needs vetting).

Telemetry and triage commands (quick reference):
- dmesg | tail -n 200 | egrep "NVRM|GPU HANG|nvlink|Xid|fault"
- journalctl -k --since "15 minutes ago" | egrep "nvrm|nvlink|gpu|cuda" -i
- nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_model.current,driver_model.pending --format=csv
- watch -n1 nvidia-smi topo -m (observe NVLink topology flapping)
- sudo cat /sys/class/pci_bus/0000:00/device/*/ecc_correctable_count (path varies by driver)
- pstack on the stuck process (capture userspace backtrace)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NVLink negotiation edge-case: when certain peer links see transient noise (fabric retrain), driver state-machine gets stuck waiting for link confirmation; GPU scheduling stalls while the driver watchdog waits. Strong correlation on boards with multiple NVLink bridges.
2) Driver watchdog bug exposed by a mixed-frequency workload pattern at low memory pressure — a race in the GPU DMA path causes an ioctl to block indefinitely.
3) ECC bursts are a downstream symptom (thermal or power noise) not primary cause for hang, but they accelerate state corruption and make driver recovery less deterministic.
4) Kernel+driver interaction: newer kernel line (6.1) changed PCIe link suspend semantics leading to timeouts during NVLink retrain.

Short experiments to run (nightly window):
- Canary group: reroute a small subset of low-risk hosts to driver 535.x for 72h and measure hang rate vs control. Owner: Jordan.
- NVLink stress test: repeatedly link-train peers in lab using nvlink-inject (fabric test harness) and capture driver trace. Owner: Luca.
- ECC scrub offload: test workload with ECC scrubbing disabled (where safe) to see if hang frequency changes. Owner: Priya.

Runbook sketch (to be refined into playbook):
Trigger: GPU hang detection (Xid 31/43 equivalents) or driver watchdog > 60s.
1) Triage: tag node as "hang-corral" in SRE dashboard; page on-call.
2) Containment: drain node (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) to prevent new tasks from scheduling.
3) Attempt driver soft-reset: sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <gpu_id> (if supported). If reset succeeds and GPUs return healthy, wait 10m and uncordon; monitor 30m.
4) If reset unsupported or fails: collect logs (dmesg, /var/log/syslog, nvidia-bug-report.sh) and perform controlled reboot (systemctl reboot). Note: ensure notification to infra SAs as reboot can trigger downstream storage reconnect flaps.
5) Post-reboot: run nvlink topo, nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS, ECC counter baseline, and run a short synthetic workload (stress test) for 10m before reintroducing to pool.

Rollback / escalation rules:
- If the same node experiences >2 hangs within a week after remediation, mark as "HW suspect" and migrate all tenants to spare capacity; open SRE-3421 with HW tag and escalate to vendor support.
- If hangs drop to near-zero on canary driver 535.x, plan a staged driver rollback across similar topology hosts.

Observability additions requested (quick wins):
- Alert: custom Prometheus rule for gpu_driver_block_time > 30s on any node (currently missing).
- Log parse: dmesg parser to extract NVLink training failure lines and Xid codes into Loki with labels (gpu_id, node, driver).
- Add ECC burst counter time-series by GPU (5s resolution) to correlate pre-hang spikes.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some boards show large ECC bursts minutes prior while others show none? (power rail, seating, DIMM-style VRAM differences?)
- Are firmware versions on NVLink bridges consistent across affected hosts? Need inventory.
- Are there subtle workload patterns that trigger it (small ephemeral FFN-heavy kernels scheduled every few seconds)? We need per-pod scheduling traces.

Immediate action items (owners & dates):
- Jordan: begin 535.x canary on 6 nodes (dup topologies) 2028-05-10 -> 2028-05-13.
- Priya: capture a 24h ECC burst/temperature trace on affected pool; add Grafana dashboard row. Due 2028-05-11.
- Luca: lab NVLink stress harness run and driver trace capture. Due 2028-05-12.
- Mei: formalize runbook steps into playbook YAML and add to oncall runbooks; add Prometheus alert. Due 2028-05-16.

Notes to firmware/vendor team:
- Collect NVLink bridge firmware versions and serials for nodes A12..A18 (we've extracted these from lspci and vendor tool). Suspect bridge firmware mismatch may cause mis-negotiation.
- Share driver trace logs (attached linked_artifacts) and request vendor triage focusing on link training state machine.

Raw log snippets (sanitized):
- "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:04:00): 31: Perf: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:04:00): 43: GPU exception: EC 32, ... driver thread timed out"
- "nvlink: link training failed on port 3: timeout while waiting for train response"

Notes to oncall: when you page, include node id, driver version, dmesg tail, and whether nvidia-smi --gpu-reset succeeds. If you are uncertain, follow containment (drain) first and escalate to second oncall for reboot decision.

This document is intentionally informal — preserve the raw investigative thread here. Will convert to a formal runbook and postmortem once experiments complete and we have cross-checks from vendor.

End of notes.
